narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall career experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have longer track records, so the system sees your limited experience as a warning sign that you may not remain with the company long-term.

The second most important factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities strongly pushes the prediction toward leaving, as it suggests you have attractive alternatives available.

Your employment in the “other” sector category also contributed to the decision, though less strongly. While this sector makes up about 22% of employees the model predicts will stay, it still nudged the outcome slightly toward departure compared to sectors like medical or education.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your high emotional commitment, recognition from superiors, and useful training you received.

The organization should consider whether additional support or clearer career paths could help retain talented people like you earlier in their careers. You may want to discuss your external opportunities and growth expectations openly with your manager to see if adjustments can be made. (218 words)
